doc.buttons: button pace: { "pauseMs" } (below: Pace); left out — unchanged
doc.lamps: devices with their signals (below); left out — unchanged

lamp.id: identifier from the export — by it the import changes the same device; without it (or with an identifier that is not here, e.g. from another account) a new one is created
lamp.key: a short name the timer actions in this document point to ("@key"): letters, digits, - _ . (up to 40 characters), unique — not saved
lamp.name: name, e.g. „Bedroom lamp” — a name or a number is required
lamp.number: device number as text, e.g. "3" (orders the buttons); null — no number
lamp.note: a note on the protocol (manufacturer, remote address, what the bytes mean) or null
lamp.protocol: "ble-adv" — raw (legacy) BLE advertisement; the only protocol, may be left out
lamp.remove: true — deletes the device together with its signals (only with "id"); timers using them will stop running them — the list of changes warns

signal.id: the signal's identifier from the export (within the device) — by it the import changes the same signal; without it a new one is created
signal.key: a short name of the signal for timer actions ("@key"), unique within the device — not saved
signal.label: the button label, e.g. „On” (required)
signal.frames: frames sent one after another, 1 to {max} (below); given ones replace all frames of the signal

frame.hex: the whole BLE advertisement packet in hex, as in nRF Connect: "1EFF0000…"; the import removes spaces, colons, commas and 0x
frame.gapMs: pause before the next frame, 0–{max} ms (default 0; meaningless after the last)

timer.id: identifier from the export — by it the import changes the same timer; without it a new one is created
timer.name: name, e.g. „Morning” (optional; without it — „Timer 07:00”)
timer.time: time "HH:MM" by the phone's clock, e.g. "06:45" — required for a new timer
timer.days: days of the week: 1–7 (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday) or "pn", "wt", "śr", "cz", "pt", "so", "nd"; [] — every day
timer.pace: this timer's pace: { "pauseMs", "limitMs" } (below); left out for a new one — fastest
timer.actions: actions sent one after another, 1 to {max} (below); given ones replace all actions of the timer

action.lamp: device: "@key" from this document, "id" from the export, or the device's name or number („Bedroom lamp”, "no. 3")
action.signal: a signal of THAT device: "@key", "id" or the button label („On”)

pace.pauseMs: pause between transmissions, 0–{max} ms: between packets in a frame (a packet every 100 ms + pause), between frames and between actions; 0 — no pause
pace.limitMs: only in a timer: transmit each frame for at most this many ms (at least {min}); null — as long as saved

node.intro:
Lamps are Bluetooth LE devices controlled by a phone with the REcreatio app (the SMS edition for Android): each device has buttons — signals, i.e. BLE advertisement packets entered by hand or read from the remote. Timers send signals at a set time. A document may contain everything (a backup, a move to another account) or only a part — e.g. just timers prepared by AI.
What the import does:
- It first shows the list of changes with warnings; only „Import” saves. Saving goes the same way as a change by hand: devices and timers are encrypted in the browser with the key of the „Only me” area, and the phone that runs the timers gets the new plan right away.
- An entry with an "id" from the export is changed in place — only the keys the document gives; the rest stays as it was. An entry without "id" (or with an "id" that is not here — e.g. from another account) is created as new, with a new "id" — on every import again, so take a fresh export for further changes.
- It deletes nothing unless an entry with "id" has "remove": true — a device, a signal or a timer; the list of changes shows it.
- An entry with an error (bad packet, no time, action without a device) is skipped with a warning; the rest is saved. Unknown keys also give a warning.
- Whether THIS phone runs the timers is set on the phone (the timer list) — the document does not contain it.
Limits: at most {rows} devices and timers together, {signals} signals in a device, {frames} frames in a signal, {actions} actions in a timer.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- Devices and timers live in your „Only me” area, each sealed separately: only you see them, on every device where you sign in; the service only sees that they exist.
- Only a phone with the app in the SMS edition transmits (Bluetooth LE advertisement). In the browser and in the regular app, devices, signals and timers can be set up but not transmitted.
- A timer remembers the device and the signal, not the bytes: a corrected signal also applies in timers as soon as the phone stores the new plan.
- The phone keeps its own timer plan, and the alarm transmits on time — even when the app is closed; „Recent runs” are shown in the timer list on the phone.
- The plan is stored anew after every change made on this phone (also after an import) and when the app starts: an import done in the browser is picked up by the phone the next time the app is opened.
- The button pace ("buttons") is remembered on the account: it applies at once to every press, on every phone; it does not change timers.

frame.title: Frame ("frames[]")
frame.lead: A frame is one packet and how long to transmit it; the frames of a signal go one after another.
frame.text: A packet is a „legacy” BLE advertisement: at most {max} bytes, with one manufacturer data structure — length, FF, manufacturer ID (2 bytes, little endian), data; e.g. "1EFF0000…" is {bytes} with ID 0x0000. The phone does not transmit other structures (flags, names, UUIDs, service data) — the import skips a signal with them. Zeros at the end (padding from listening) are not transmitted.

signal.title: Signal ("signals[]")
signal.lead: A signal is a button: a label and what the phone transmits when it is pressed — one frame or several in order (a sequence). A short press sends the whole signal; holding transmits while the button is held.
signal.text: The import skips a signal with an error (e.g. a bad packet) with a warning — a change to an existing signal is then not applied; the rest of the device is saved.

lamp.title: Device ("lamps[]")
lamp.lead: A device orders the buttons: name, number and room do not select a receiver — a BLE advertisement reaches every lamp in range, and which one switches on is decided by the bytes in the packet.
lamp.text: Signals of an existing device: with "id" they change in place, without "id" they are added, unlisted ones stay. When the document lists ALL signals of the device, its order applies; when only some — new ones are added at the end. Devices appear on the page by number, then by name.

action.title: Timer action ("actions[]")
action.lead: Action: which signal of which device to send.
action.text: "@key" is the "key" of a device or signal in this document; the key the export gives a device and signal (e.g. "@lampa-w-sypialni-nr-1", "@wlacz") also works when the device itself is not in the document. Names are compared ignoring case and Polish characters; a name must point to exactly one device (one signal) — otherwise the action is skipped with a warning. The export writes actions as "@key".

pace.title: Pace ("pace", "buttons")
pace.lead: Pace slows transmission without changing the saved signals. In a timer: { "pauseMs", "limitMs" }; in "buttons" (buttons and test sends, remembered on the account) only "pauseMs" — how long a button transmits is decided by holding it.

timer.title: Timer ("timers[]")
timer.lead: A timer sends signals in order at a given time on chosen days of the week. It is run by a phone with the REcreatio app (SMS edition) on which timers are switched on — even when the app is closed.
timer.text: To change an existing timer, "id" and what changes are enough (e.g. {"id": "…", "enabled": false}). The import skips a timer with a bad time, bad days or no action that points to something (an existing one stays unchanged).
